reasoning_summary: Steps 0001-0060 check out. The Thue-Mahler framing (0005-0009) and the quoted Bugeaud-Gyory bound n <= P+1 with P = max{p_1,...,p_r,3} (0016-0024) are used correctly. The reduction to coprime solutions (0026-0030) is legitimate because passing to the free-exponent Thue-Mahler form only enlarges the solution set. In 0032-0039 the condition phi(y) > P_y + 1 is correctly rewritten: c_y P_y^{k-1}(P_y-1) > P_y+1 iff (c_y P_y^{k-1} - 1)(P_y - 1) > 2. Since P_y >= 3 gives P_y - 1 >= 2, failure of that inequality forces c_y P_y^{k-1} <= 2, hence k=1 with c_y=1, or k=1, c_y=2, P_y=3; translating via phi(y/P_y) = c_y gives exactly y in {12} u {2^k : k>2} u {p, 2p}, so 0040-0043 are right. The y=p^e dismissal (0044) is standard: both factors x^n +/- z^n are p-powers, their gcd forces x^n - z^n in {1,2}, impossible for n >= 2 with z >= 1. The y=12 case (0046-0050) is correct: squares mod 3 are {0,1} and mod 4 are {0,1}, so coprimality forbids 3 | xi^2+zeta^2 and 4 | xi^2+zeta^2, leaving xi^2+zeta^2 = 2 and the contradiction xi^4 - zeta^4 = 0. For y=2p the WLOG in 0052, the factorization in 0054, the fact that p divides only one of xi^f +/- zeta^f in 0056 (else p | 2xi^f and p | 2zeta^f, contradicting gcd=1 for odd p), and the size contradiction in 0058-0060 (xi^f - zeta^f < xi^f + zeta^f <= 2^tau < p^tau <= xi^f - zeta^f) are all valid, so xi^f - zeta^f = 2^sigma. Step 0062 then fails: applying the quoted theorem to xi^f - zeta^f = 2^sigma uses the single prime 2, so P = max{2,3} = 3 and the bound is f <= P+1 = 4, i.e. (p-1)/2 <= 4, i.e. p <= 9. The surviving primes p > 3 are p = 5 (f = 2, where the theorem does not even apply since it requires n >= 3) and p = 7 (f = 3, which satisfies f <= 4 and is therefore not excluded). The proof asserts that only p = 5 remains, silently dropping p = 7; no argument anywhere in the proof rules out f = 3. The final case analysis is thus incomplete and the stated conclusion at that step does not follow.
